title: Lapsed Settlement Offers and the Lump-Sum Settlement Percent: Collections Academy Note
content:
**The rule.** On an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts, the lump-sum lapsed offers are the account's lump-sum settlement and installment settlement offers with the status expired or declined whose offer date falls fewer than 12 whole months before today. Two or more add 4.0 percentage points to the lump-sum settlement percent, exactly one adds 2.0 points, and none adds no points. Whole months are counted as the difference in calendar months between the two dates, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

## Questions answered by the rule

**Which offers count?** Settlement offers only, of either kind, that the borrower declined or let expire. Payment-plan offers never count, and neither do settlement offers that were accepted, broken or completed.

**Which dates count?** The offer date. Today being the 15th of a month, an offer dated the 16th of the same month a year earlier is 11 whole months back and counts; one dated the 15th of that month a year earlier is 12 whole months back and does not.

**Do three lapsed offers add more than two?** No; two or more add 4.0 points.

| Lapsed settlement offers in the look-back | Points added |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 4.0 |
| Exactly one | 2.0 |
| None | None |
